lesson_scope: Tangents to circles from an external point and using the discriminant method: setting Delta = 0 for intersection quadratic, finding tangent gradients, points of contact, chord of contact, and areas of tangent triangles and squares.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: finding length of tangent segment from external point using Pythagoras.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of tangent segment length from external point.

hints: Use Pythagoras in right-angled triangle $\triangle TCP$: $TP = \sqrt{TC^2 - r^2} = \sqrt{25 - 9} = 4$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the squared distance from external point $T(5, 5)$ to centre $C(1, 2)$:
$$TC^2 = (5 - 1)^2 + (5 - 2)^2 = 4^2 + 3^2 = 25$$

Use the right-angled triangle formed by radius $CP = 3$ and tangent segment $TP$:
$$TP = \sqrt{TC^2 - r^2} = \sqrt{25 - 9} = \sqrt{16} = 4$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: applying discriminant tangency condition to determine y-intercept c.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of discriminant tangency condition on c.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute $y = 2x + c$ into the circle equation:
$$x^2 + (2x + c)^2 = 5$$
$$x^2 + 4x^2 + 4cx + c^2 - 5 = 0$$
$$5x^2 + 4cx + (c^2 - 5) = 0$$

Set the discriminant equal to zero for tangency:
$$\Delta = (4c)^2 - 4(5)(c^2 - 5) = 0$$
$$16c^2 - 20c^2 + 100 = 0$$
$$-4c^2 + 100 = 0 \implies c^2 = 25 \implies c = 5 \quad \text{or} \quad c = -5$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: finding tangent gradients from an external point on y-axis using discriminant.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of finding tangent gradients from external point.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute line equation $y = mx + 5$ into circle $x^2 + y^2 = 9$:
$$x^2 + (mx + 5)^2 = 9$$
$$(1 + m^2)x^2 + 10mx + 16 = 0$$

Apply the tangency condition $\Delta = 0$:
$$\Delta = (10m)^2 - 4(1 + m^2)(16) = 0$$
$$100m^2 - 64 - 64m^2 = 0$$
$$36m^2 = 64 \implies m^2 = \dfrac{64}{36} = \dfrac{16}{9} \implies m = \pm \dfrac{4}{3}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Substitutes $y = mx + 5$ into $x^2 + y^2 = 9$ and sets $\Delta = 100m^2 - 64(1 + m^2) = 0$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: finding tangent gradients from origin to a shifted circle.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of tangents through origin to circle.

hints: Lines through the origin have equation $y = mx$.

walkthrough.text:
Set the discriminant to zero for tangency:
$$\Delta = (-10)^2 - 4(1 + m^2)(16) = 0$$
$$100 - 64 - 64m^2 = 0$$
$$64m^2 = 36 \implies m^2 = \dfrac{36}{64} = \dfrac{9}{16} \implies m = \pm \dfrac{3}{4}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Substitutes $y = mx$ into $(x - 5)^2 + y^2 = 9$ and sets $\Delta = 100 - 64(1 + m^2) = 0$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of finding tangent contact point.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the corresponding $y$-coordinate:
$$y = 2(-2) + 5 = 1$$
$$\text{Point of contact: } (-2, 1)$$

ai_rubric.observable: Evaluates $y = 2(-2) + 5 = 1$ to give point of contact $(-2, 1)$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of parallel tangents to circle.

hints: The lines are $y = 3x + c \implies 3x - y + c = 0$.
The distance from centre $(2, 3)$ to $3x - y + c = 0$ must equal radius $r = \sqrt{10}$.
Use perpendicular distance formula: $\dfrac{|3(2) - 3 + c|}{\sqrt{3^2 + (-1)^2}} = \sqrt{10} \implies |3 + c| = 10 \implies c = 7 \text{ or } c = -13$.

walkthrough.text:
The tangent lines have equation $3x - y + c = 0$. The perpendicular distance from centre $(2, 3)$ to the line equals radius $\sqrt{10}$:
$$\dfrac{|3(2) - (3) + c|}{\sqrt{3^2 + (-1)^2}} = \sqrt{10}$$
$$\dfrac{|3 + c|}{\sqrt{10}} = \sqrt{10} \implies |3 + c| = 10$$

Solve for the two possible values of $c$:
$$3 + c = 10 \implies c = 7$$
$$3 + c = -10 \implies c = -13$$
$$y = 3x + 7 \quad \text{and} \quad y = 3x - 13$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sets up distance condition $\dfrac{|3(2) - 3 + c|}{\sqrt{10}} = \sqrt{10} \implies |3 + c| = 10$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Easy: verifying external point relative to circle and computing tangent segment length via Pythagoras.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Checking external point position.

hints: Since $100 > 25$, conclude that $T(11, 5)$ lies outside the circle.

walkthrough.text:
Extract centre $C(3, -1)$ and calculate the squared distance $TC^2$:
$$TC^2 = (11 - 3)^2 + (5 - (-1))^2 = 8^2 + 6^2 = 64 + 36 = 100$$

Compare $TC^2$ with $r^2 = 25$:
$$100 > 25 \implies TC > r$$
$$\text{Therefore, } T(11, 5) \text{ lies strictly outside the circle } C.$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding tangent segment length.

hints: The triangle $\triangle TCA$ has right angle at $A$ (radius perpendicular to tangent).

walkthrough.text:
Apply Pythagoras in right-angled triangle $\triangle TCA$ with hypotenuse $TC$:
$$TC^2 = CA^2 + TA^2$$
$$100 = 25 + TA^2 \implies TA^2 = 75$$

Evaluate the exact tangent length:
$$TA = \sqrt{75} = 5\sqrt{3}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Applies Pythagoras in $\triangle TCA$: $TA^2 = TC^2 - r^2 = 100 - 25 = 75$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Easy: forming quadratic in x for line y = mx + 5 and circle x^2 + y^2 = 16, and solving discriminant for tangent gradients.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Forming quadratic from line and circle substitution.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute $y = mx + 5$ into the circle equation $x^2 + y^2 = 16$:
$$x^2 + (mx + 5)^2 = 16$$

Expand and collect like terms to obtain the quadratic in $x$:
$$x^2 + m^2x^2 + 10mx + 25 - 16 = 0$$
$$(1 + m^2)x^2 + 10mx + 9 = 0$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding tangent gradients using discriminant.

walkthrough.text:
Set the discriminant to zero for tangency:
$$\Delta = (10m)^2 - 4(1 + m^2)(9) = 0$$
$$100m^2 - 36(1 + m^2) = 0$$
$$100m^2 - 36m^2 - 36 = 0$$

Solve for $m$:
$$64m^2 = 36 \implies m^2 = \dfrac{36}{64} = \dfrac{9}{16}$$
$$m = \dfrac{3}{4} \quad \text{or} \quad m = -\dfrac{3}{4}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Medium: finding tangent gradients from origin to circle (x - 4)^2 + y^2 = 4 and calculating exact contact coordinates.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding tangent gradients from origin to circle.

walkthrough.text:
Apply the tangency condition $\Delta = 0$:
$$\Delta = (-8)^2 - 4(1 + m^2)(12) = 0$$
$$64 - 48 - 48m^2 = 0$$
$$16 - 48m^2 = 0 \implies 3m^2 - 1 = 0 \implies m = \pm \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Substitutes $y = mx$ to get $(1 + m^2)x^2 - 8x + 12 = 0$ and sets $\Delta = 64 - 48(1 + m^2) = 0$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding contact points of tangents from origin.

hints: The $x$-coordinate of the contact point is the repeated root: $x = -\dfrac{b}{2a} = \dfrac{8}{2(1 + 1/3)} = \dfrac{8}{8/3} = 3$.

walkthrough.text:
For a tangent, the quadratic $(1 + m^2)x^2 - 8x + 12 = 0$ has a repeated root $x = -\dfrac{b}{2a}$:
$$x = \dfrac{8}{2(1 + m^2)} = \dfrac{8}{2(1 + 1/3)} = \dfrac{8}{8/3} = 3$$

Substitute $x = 3$ into the tangent equations $y = mx$:
$$\text{For } m = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}: \quad y = \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{3}} = \sqrt{3} \implies P(3, \sqrt{3})$$
$$\text{For } m = -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}: \quad y = -\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{3}} = -\sqrt{3} \implies Q(3, -\sqrt{3})$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Medium: parameter determination in circle equation using tangency condition on y = 2x + 7.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Forming quadratic with circle parameter.

walkthrough.text:
Expand and collect coefficients in descending powers of $x$:
$$(x^2 - 2ax + a^2) + (4x^2 + 24x + 36) - 20 = 0$$
$$5x^2 + (24 - 2a)x + (a^2 + 16) = 0$$

ai_rubric.observable: Substitutes $y = 2x + 7$ into $(x - a)^2 + (y - 1)^2 = 20$ to get $(x - a)^2 + (2x + 6)^2 = 20$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding circle parameter via discriminant.

walkthrough.text:
Divide through by $-16$ and factorise:
$$a^2 + 6a - 16 = 0$$
$$(a + 8)(a - 2) = 0$$
$$\text{Since } a > 0, \quad a = 2$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Medium: finding perpendicular diameter to parallel tangents and determining equations of both parallel tangents.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding diameter perpendicular to parallel tangents.

hints: The tangents have gradient $2$, so the perpendicular diameter has gradient $m_\perp = -\dfrac{1}{2}$.
The diameter passes through the circle centre $(3, -2)$.

walkthrough.text:
The diameter through the points of contact is perpendicular to the tangents of gradient $2$:
$$m_{\text{diam}} = -\dfrac{1}{2}$$

The diameter passes through the centre $(3, -2)$:
$$y - (-2) = -\dfrac{1}{2}(x - 3)$$
$$2y + 4 = -x + 3 \implies x + 2y + 1 = 0$$

ai_rubric.observable: Uses perpendicular gradient $m_\perp = -\dfrac{1}{2}$ through circle centre $(3, -2)$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding equations of parallel tangents.

hints: So $y + 2 = \pm 2 \implies y = 0$ or $y = -4$. Points of contact are $(-1, 0)$ and $(7, -4)$ (or $(1, -1)$ and $(5, -3)$ depending on substitution).

walkthrough.text:
Find the contact points by intersecting the diameter $x = -2y - 1$ with the circle:
$$(-2y - 1 - 3)^2 + (y + 2)^2 = 20$$
$$(-2(y + 2))^2 + (y + 2)^2 = 20$$
$$4(y + 2)^2 + (y + 2)^2 = 20 \implies 5(y + 2)^2 = 20 \implies (y + 2)^2 = 4$$
$$y + 2 = 2 \implies y = 0, \quad x = -1 \implies (-1, 0)$$
$$y + 2 = -2 \implies y = -4, \quad x = 7 \implies (7, -4)$$

Write the equations of the tangents with gradient $2$ at both contact points:
$$L_1: \quad y - 0 = 2(x - (-1)) \implies y = 2x + 2$$
$$L_2: \quad y - (-4) = 2(x - 7) \implies y + 4 = 2x - 14 \implies y = 2x - 18$$

ai_rubric.observable: Finds contact points by intersecting diameter with circle: $(1, -1)$ and $(5, -3)$.
Writes tangent equations $y - (-1) = 2(x - 1) \implies y = 2x - 3 + 5 = 2x - 3 + ... \implies y = 2x + 2$ and $y - (-3) = 2(x - 5) \implies y = 2x - 18$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Hard: finding tangent gradients from T(0,10) to x^2 + y^2 = 20, contact points, chord of contact, and area of triangle TAB.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding tangent gradients and contact points from external point.

walkthrough.text:
Lines through $T(0, 10)$ have equation $y = mx + 10$. Substitute into $x^2 + y^2 = 20$:
$$x^2 + (mx + 10)^2 = 20$$
$$(1 + m^2)x^2 + 20mx + 80 = 0$$

Set discriminant $\Delta = 0$ for tangency:
$$\Delta = (20m)^2 - 4(1 + m^2)(80) = 0$$
$$400m^2 - 320(1 + m^2) = 0$$
$$80m^2 = 320 \implies m^2 = 4 \implies m = 2 \quad \text{or} \quad m = -2$$

Find the contact points from the repeated root formula $x = -\dfrac{b}{2a}$:
$$\text{For } m = 2: \quad x = -\dfrac{40}{2(5)} = -4, \quad y = 2(-4) + 10 = 2 \implies A(-4, 2)$$
$$\text{For } m = -2: \quad x = -\dfrac{-40}{2(5)} = 4, \quad y = -2(4) + 10 = 2 \implies B(4, 2)$$

ai_rubric.observable: Substitutes $y = mx + 10$ into $x^2 + y^2 = 20$ to form $(1 + m^2)x^2 + 20mx + 80 = 0$.
Finds contact points $x = -\dfrac{20m}{2(1 + m^2)} = -2m \implies A(-4, 2)$ and $B(4, 2)$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding chord of contact and triangle area.

hints: Both $A(-4, 2)$ and $B(4, 2)$ share $y = 2$, so chord $AB$ is the horizontal line $y = 2$.

walkthrough.text:
The points $A(-4, 2)$ and $B(4, 2)$ both lie on the horizontal line:
$$\text{Chord } AB: \quad y = 2$$

Calculate the area of triangle $TAB$ with base $AB$ and vertical altitude from $T(0, 10)$:
$$\text{Base } AB = 4 - (-4) = 8$$
$$\text{Height } h = 10 - 2 = 8$$
$$\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 8 \times 8 = 32$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Hard: deriving quadratic in gradient m from general external point T(7,1), proving perpendicularity, finding contact points, and evaluating quadrilateral area.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding tangent gradients from general external point.

hints: Lines through $T(7, 1)$ have equation $y - 1 = m(x - 7) \implies mx - y + (1 - 7m) = 0$.
The distance from origin $(0, 0)$ to the tangent equals radius $r = 5$: $\dfrac{|1 - 7m|}{\sqrt{1 + m^2}} = 5$.

walkthrough.text:
A line through $T(7, 1)$ has equation $y - 1 = m(x - 7)$, or $mx - y + (1 - 7m) = 0$. The perpendicular distance from centre $(0, 0)$ to the tangent line equals the radius $r = 5$:
$$\dfrac{|m(0) - 0 + (1 - 7m)|}{\sqrt{m^2 + (-1)^2}} = 5$$
$$\dfrac{|1 - 7m|}{\sqrt{1 + m^2}} = 5$$

Square both sides and simplify to form the quadratic in $m$:
$$(1 - 7m)^2 = 25(1 + m^2)$$
$$1 - 14m + 49m^2 = 25 + 25m^2$$
$$24m^2 - 14m - 24 = 0 \implies 12m^2 - 7m - 12 = 0$$

Factorise and find the equations of the two tangents:
$$(3m - 4)(4m + 3) = 0 \implies m = \dfrac{4}{3} \quad \text{or} \quad m = -\dfrac{3}{4}$$
$$\text{For } m = \dfrac{4}{3}: \quad y - 1 = \dfrac{4}{3}(x - 7) \implies 4x - 3y = 25$$
$$\text{For } m = -\dfrac{3}{4}: \quad y - 1 = -\dfrac{3}{4}(x - 7) \implies 3x + 4y = 25$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sets distance from $(0, 0)$ to $mx - y + (1 - 7m) = 0$ equal to $5$: $\dfrac{|1 - 7m|}{\sqrt{1 + m^2}} = 5$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Proving perpendicular tangents and finding quadrilateral area.

hints: Observe $m_1 \times m_2 = \dfrac{4}{3} \times \left(-\dfrac{3}{4}\right) = -1$, showing the tangents are perpendicular.
Normal lines through $(0, 0)$ have gradients $-\dfrac{3}{4}$ and $\dfrac{4}{3}$: $A(4, -3)$ and $B(3, 4)$.
The quadrilateral $CATB$ has four right angles and adjacent sides of equal length $r = 5$, so it is a square of side $5$.

walkthrough.text:
Verify the perpendicularity of the tangents:
$$m_1 \times m_2 = \dfrac{4}{3} \times \left(-\dfrac{3}{4}\right) = -1 \implies \text{The two tangents meet at } 90^\circ \text{ at } T$$

Find the contact points $A$ and $B$:
$$\text{Normal to } 4x - 3y = 25: \quad y = -\dfrac{3}{4}x \implies x^2 + \dfrac{9}{16}x^2 = 25 \implies x = 4, y = -3 \implies A(4, -3)$$
$$\text{Normal to } 3x + 4y = 25: \quad y = \dfrac{4}{3}x \implies x^2 + \dfrac{16}{9}x^2 = 25 \implies x = 3, y = 4 \implies B(3, 4)$$

Since $\angle CAT = \angle CBT = \angle ATB = \angle ACB = 90^\circ$ and $CA = CB = 5$, quadrilateral $CATB$ is a square of side $5$:
$$\text{Area} = 5^2 = 25$$

ai_rubric.observable: Finds contact points $A(4, -3)$ and $B(3, 4)$ by normal gradients.
Deduces $CATB$ is a square of side length $r = 5$, giving $\text{Area} = 5^2 = 25$.
